The Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem: If a function x(t) (the sampled signal) contains no frequencies higher than B hertz, then it can be completely determined from its sampled values at a sequence of points spaced less than 1/(2B)seconds apart.
In other words, the lower sampling rate is twice the smaller frequency to be analyzed.
